meta.title: Omkar Ajagunde ✳ Development Lead, AI Tooling

hero.name: Omkar
hero.intro: I lead development of AI tooling at IBM, for seller and developer productivity in the CIO department. Below is what I do and how I work.
hero.photoAlt: Omkar in a navy sweater at a café

chapters.title: Development Lead, AI Tooling.
chapters.body: At IBM I lead development of AI tooling for seller and developer productivity in the CIO department. Other teams build chatbots and agents. My team takes care of the common pieces so they can <mark>focus on their business logic and their agents' tools</mark>. We handle RAG, user experience, feedback collection and <mark>measuring whether a chatbot is actually giving business value</mark>.

chapters.title: IBM, Bengaluru.
chapters.body: I'm from Pune and now work out of IBM's Bengaluru office. <mark>Building things was a hobby first</mark>, and now it's my job.

chapters.alt: Omkar posing by a tall white door
chapters.title: B.E., Information Technology.
chapters.body: I did my B.E. in Information Technology. Most of what I know though, I learnt by <mark>building and shipping real software</mark>, and breaking a few things along the way. I speak Marathi and English.

chapters.alt: Omkar smiling at a wooden table
chapters.title: Side projects, from scratch.
chapters.body: Outside office work I keep building side projects. Some became real products, some didn't. Either way <mark>I learn something every time</mark>.

chapters.title: Breaks are part of it.
chapters.body: I work hard, and every few months I take a proper break and travel. <mark>I come back with a clearer head</mark>, and the work is better for it.

principles.title:
The way
I work.
principles.blurb: Five things I'm good at. Where they overlap is how I decide what to build.

items.label: AI|efficiency
items.title: I use AI tools a lot.
items.body: I use AI tools every day for my own work. By now I know <mark>where they save hours and where they waste time</mark>.

items.label: On top of|new tech
items.title: I keep up with new tech.
items.body: I pick up new tools and frameworks early. <mark>I try them myself first</mark>, and suggest them to the team only if they're actually useful.

items.label: Multi-|tasking
items.title: I can handle many things at once.
items.body: Most days I'm running <mark>several streams of work in parallel</mark>, and I make sure none of them gets stuck.

items.label: Asks →|implementation
items.title: Requirements to working code.
items.body: Stakeholders tell me what they need. I think it through, ask the questions nobody asked, and <mark>turn it into something we can build and ship</mark>.

items.label: Business|sense
items.title: I understand the business side.
items.body: So I look at problems <mark>use case first, customer first, and with cost in mind</mark>. Using new tech just because it's new doesn't make sense to me.

projects.title:
Things I've
built.
projects.blurb: Products, side projects, client work and college projects, newest first. Tap a preview to open it.

items.title: Bato.club
items.body: A Splitwise-style app for <mark>tracking shared expenses, splitting bills and settling up</mark>, without sending awkward reminders to friends. It's live on the web, App Store and Play Store.

stats.label: in expenses tracked since launch in July 2026

items.title: Lighthouse
items.body: One platform where <mark>architects, designers and brands connect, work together and get leads</mark>. It has an RFQ marketplace where buyers ask for quotes and dealers respond. I built most of the backend, along with AI agents that keep the product catalogue updated.

items.title: BeeGuide
items.body: A tool to <mark>create product tours for web apps</mark>. It has a Chrome extension to record tours, a site with docs and tour management, and a script to add the tours to your own website.

items.title: Blablah.app
items.body: A <mark>realtime chat app</mark> with server-side rendering, built on sockets with Redis on the backend.

items.title: 360nearme
items.body: See places near you as <mark>360° panoramas</mark>, right in the browser, using Pannellum.

items.title: Core2web professional network
items.body: A <mark>professional network for the Core2web community</mark>, made as a responsive React app.

items.title: Dummy data filler
items.body: A Chrome extension that <mark>fills forms with fake but realistic data</mark>. Saves a lot of time while testing.

items.title: Sorting visualiser
items.body: Shows <mark>sorting algorithms running step by step</mark>, in plain JavaScript.

items.title: Data extraction with YOLOv3
items.body: My final year project. <mark>Pulling structured data out of images using a neural network</mark>, with a Flask API and a React front end.

items.title: Attendance by face recognition
items.body: A desktop app that <mark>marks attendance by recognising faces</mark>.

items.title: Win32 graphics demo
items.body: A <mark>graphics demo using the raw Win32 GDI APIs</mark>, written in C and C++.

items.title: TeslaBox@core2web
items.body: An <mark>IoT box built on the ESP8266</mark> that reads IR and gas sensors over I2C and SPI.

hello.title: Working on something interesting? Tell me about it.
paragraphs: AI tooling, developer productivity, or some problem that's still not clear, I'm happy to talk about it.
Email is the easiest way to reach me.
